thread:
incident-bot: P0 alert: privateconnect/PrivateLink AZ-B path flap detected — multiple customers report 503s and TCP resets. Auto-escalation to oncall triggered. Links: https://infra.redwood/pager/2705009999 :rotating_light:
Micah (oncall): I'm on it, acknowledging. Paging netops + infra. Micah (oncall): initial check — control plane OK, but dataplane shows repeated route withdrawals in AZ-B to our PrivateLink VIPs. Seeing ~200 route withdraws in last 5m. Jordan (netops): I see the same from the BGP collector — neighbor 10.4.0.1 flapping, AS path toggling between local and remote. show output: ```
BGP neighbor 10.4.0.1
  State: Established, Up for 00:03:24
  Last reset reason: hold timer expired
  Prefixes advertised: 120
  Flap count: 38
```
Micah (oncall): Any config pushes in AZ-B? Priya (infra): No infra deploys in AZ-B in the window. We did a kernel upgrade yesterday on some hosts but not scheduled for today. Aleena (CSE): Multiple customers (acme-corp, beta-saas) reporting errors after they hit PrivateLink endpoints. They say DNS resolves but connections close mid-handshake.
Jordan (netops): Hypothesis: asymmetric routing / wrong next-hop after a route withdraw is causing connection reset when returning via transit. I can attempt a targeted neighbor shutdown to stop the flap and force path selection to the healthy route. Micah (oncall): Do it if safe. Notify downstream providers first.
Jordan (netops): Rolling now: `bgp neighbor 10.4.0.1 shutdown` -> pause. Notifying provider ops: @provider-ops slack msg sent. Micah (oncall): Switching a subset of PrivateLink frontends to public fallback for impacted customers to restore immediate connectivity. Aleena (CSE): I'll inform the customers that we're failing them over to a fallback for minimal disruption and will update.
DeployBot: Canary rollback triggered for PL-vip-proxy group in AZ-B -> rolling to fallback config (60s between hosts). Micah (oncall): Observing metrics — 503s for acme-corp drop from 17/s to 2/s within 90s. TCP resets down to baseline. Priya (infra): We're still seeing DNS TTL churn for PrivateLink hostnames in AZ-B — likely due to route instability causing some resolvers to prefer alternative IPs. Jordan (netops): Running packet capture on a host in AZ-B to confirm asymmetric path: `sudo tcpdump -w /tmp/azb-flap.pcap host 10.200.5.10 and port 443`
Micah (oncall): Putting customer impact summary together for status page: impacted customers: acme-corp, beta-saas, gamma-analytics (partial). Impact: intermittent 5xx and connection resets to PrivateLink endpoints in AZ-B; some retries transparent to clients. ETA to mitigation: immediate fallback deployed, full route stabilization pending.
Jordan (netops): Provider acknowledged transient BGP instability; they applied soft-reconfiguration. I'm seeing fewer withdraws now — flap count stabilizing. Show: ```
Flap count: 3
Last reset reason: BGP peer 10.4.0.1 admin down -> cleared
```
Micah (oncall): Next: keep fallback active for 30m, monitor metrics, plan controlled re-enable of neighbor once peer confirms stable for 10m. Priya (infra): I'll keep an eye on DNS TTL and run a sweep to clear any stale local caches: `sudo rndc flush` and restarting resolver on edge proxies. Aleena (CSE): Customer comms sent: "We've failed over your PrivateLink endpoint to an alternate path while we stabilize routing. Expected no data loss; please report if you see persistent errors."
Micah (oncall): Handing off to Jordan for the next 30m monitoring window. If routes stable for 10m, re-enable prior neighbor. Leaving a note in incident tracker. Jordan (netops): Taking over monitoring. If we see flaps >3 in 10m, we'll keep fallback and escalate to provider NOC for circuit trace. Micah (oncall): Thanks — if anything critical pops, page me.
(30m later) Jordan (netops): Provider confirms the remote peer had a memory leak causing sporadic BGP resets; they pushed patch and re-established stable session. Re-enable command executed: `no neighbor 10.4.0.1 shutdown` -> BGP back to established and prefixes converged. Observed no new withdraws for 12m.
Micah (oncall): Marking incident as mitigated. Open action items: 1) postmortem to analyze why kernel upgrade hosts appeared slightly more susceptible to path churn; 2) test improved fallback automation for future PrivateLink flaps; 3) add route-targeted alerts to catch early withdraw spikes. Aleena (CSE): I'll follow up with customers with post-incident note and remediation timeline. DeployBot: Incident ticket updated with timeline and logs: https://infra.redwood/incidents/2705009999/logs
Micah (oncall): Closing oncall handoff. Great coordination. :thumbsup:
